name: Overclaim-scoping review: fix the sentence, not the code
description: Handle the MEASURED most-common adversarial outcome correctly. Across three lanes and four adversarial reviews, 5 of 8 refutations were OVERCLAIMS - the code was right and the sentence was wider than its evidence. This blueprint compares a claim's asserted scope against its evidence's actual scope and, where the claim is wider, emits the correctly-scoped replacement sentence. An overclaim is a REFUTED verdict even when the code is fine; a genuine defect must NOT be softened into a scoping note; and a residual that is honestly scoped and disclosed INLINE is not a refuted item and must not block.

claim_ref.description: The document carrying the claims under review (report, PR body, skill doc)

evidence_manifest.description: What was actually measured, so the evidence scope is readable rather than assumed

claim_selector.description: Which claims to review; CONFIRMED claims are where overclaims hide

retain_refuted_wording.description: Keep the refuted sentence in the record with a REFUTED tag rather than deleting it

scope-measurer.description: Reads the evidence manifest and states what scope it actually covers

claim-rewriter.description: Emits the correctly-scoped replacement sentence for an overclaim

defect-police.description: Guards the weasel path: a real defect must not be reclassified as a scoping note

routes.reason: the reclassification guard is the one place a soft verdict does real damage

stages.title: What does each claim actually assert?

work_unit.title: Extract each claim's asserted scope, including its implicit quantifier
work_unit.question_or_target: For every selected claim, write down the scope it asserts - the quantifier (every / all / N of M / this one case), the population, and the time window. 'recall = 1.0' asserts a universal; 'recall = 1.0 on the 20-case sample' asserts a sample. The difference is the whole review.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: quantifier extraction is a language judgement no regex makes reliably

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each claim quotes its own sentence verbatim with a file:line anchor and names its quantifier
tests_required: a bare universal ('FP=0') and a scoped one ('FP=0 over the 30 fixtures') must extract to DIFFERENT quantifiers
both-states control: a claim with no quantifier must be recorded as UNQUANTIFIED, not silently promoted to universal
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the defect-police role cross-examines any claim whose quantifier was read down
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:CRV-5301 emitted only when every selected claim carries a verbatim quote, a file:line anchor and an explicit quantifier or an UNQUANTIFIED marker; otherwise FAILED:CRV-5301 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to reviewing claims one at a time instead of in a batch
work_unit.mechanism: per-claim quantifier and population extraction from the claim text

stages.title: What does the evidence actually cover?

work_unit.title: Rewrite each overclaimed sentence to the scope its evidence actually supports
work_unit.question_or_target: For every REFUTED-OVERCLAIM, write the replacement sentence: state the scope MEASURED, disclose the residual INLINE adjacent to the claim (a trailing limitations section does not satisfy this), and name the experiment that would settle the residual. Keep the refuted wording in the record with a REFUTED tag rather than deleting it, so the dead end is retired instead of forgotten.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: rewriting to exactly the measured scope is the deliverable and needs the strong model

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each rewrite pairs the original sentence, the replacement, the measured scope, the inline residual and the settling experiment
tests_required: a 'recall = 1.0' claim backed by a 20-case sample must be rescoped to the sample, NOT rejected outright
both-states control: a rewrite whose residual sits only in a trailing limitations section must FAIL the inline-adjacency gate
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the defect-police role checks that nothing reclassified here was a genuine defect
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:CRV-5302 emitted only when every overclaim has a replacement sentence, an inline residual and a named settling experiment, and the refuted wording is retained; otherwise FAILED:CRV-5302 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to marking the claim UNRESOLVED, which is itself a scoping defect
work_unit.mechanism: sentence rewrite bounded by the measured evidence scope
work_unit.not_a_duplicate_because: an adversarial premise attack looks for a shared FALSE premise across lanes; this measures the WIDTH of one sentence against its own evidence and its output is a rewritten sentence

stages.title: A refuted overclaim without a replacement sentence is an incomplete review
The residual must sit next to the claim, not in a trailing section
Every residual names the experiment that would settle it
Cross-examine every overclaim verdict for a hidden real defect
A genuine defect may not be reclassified as a scoping note
Emit the scoping verdict only after the defect-police gate clears

impact.blast_radius: produces rewritten sentences as proposals under command-center/review/**; never edits the claim document in place

x_extensions.mechanism: Measure the quantifier a sentence asserts, measure the scope its evidence covers, and where the first exceeds the second emit a narrower sentence. The artifact is a rewritten claim, not a finding about code.
contraindications: NOT for code correctness - that is BP-CRV-01 (reading) or BP-CRV-03 (proving)
NOT where there is no claim, only code
NOT a route to soften a real defect: defect-not-softened is a veto gate for exactly that

benchmark_cases.name: sampled-recall-claim
benchmark_cases.expected: REFUTED-OVERCLAIM, rescoped to the 20-case sample - NOT rejected outright

benchmark_cases.name: genuine-defect
benchmark_cases.setup: a claim that is false because the code is wrong
benchmark_cases.expected: REFUTED-DEFECT; classing it as an overclaim is the failure this blueprint must not commit

x_extensions.why_not_a_duplicate: BP-CNC-04 attacks shared PREMISES across lanes; BP-CRV-01/03 judge code. This attacks the WIDTH of a single sentence relative to its own evidence, and its only output is a rewritten sentence.
x_extensions.measured_basis: MEASURED, not assumed: 5 of 8 refutations across three lanes and four adversarial reviews were overclaims with correct code (fan-out-contract C2). Only 3 of 8 were genuine defects and each closed in one round - which is why a 'round N until green' stopping rule is tractable.
x_extensions.unverified: UNVERIFIED (very-likely, given 5/8 measured) that the ratio reproduces; settling experiment = classify the next 8 adversarial refutations and check whether the 5-in-8 overclaim ratio holds.

worked_example.name: review the CONFIRMED claims in a completion report
worked_example.narrative: Nine CONFIRMED claims reviewed. Seven survived. One asserted 'every declared path resolves' where the manifest measured only the 234 distinct logical files, so it was rescoped to that population with the residual disclosed in the same sentence and a settling experiment named. One was a real defect and the defect-police role kept it classed REFUTED-DEFECT.

negative_control.why: the measured failure was 40% of UNVERIFIED tags sitting in the final 15% of their document; a trailing limitations section must not satisfy the disclosure requirement
